lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic identifying interests, strengths, and constraints task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner fills out a three-part inventory: activities they are genuinely curious about or enjoy, strengths they can back with a specific remembered moment rather than a guess, and real constraints on time and getting to a location that they can name honestly.
safetyNotes: No household financial detail, income, or specific address information is requested; constraints are described in general terms (for example, 'limited to weekends' or 'depends on someone else's schedule') rather than exact personal or family circumstances.
materials: learner-local: this task sheet's three-part inventory prompts

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which constraint is the biggest open question for you right now, and why does it matter for the kind of work you'd realistically be able to start?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason. | Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment. | Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner ask someone who knows them well (without naming a required relationship) to name one strength the learner didn't list, and add it to the inventory with the reason the other person gave.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic identifying interests, strengths, and constraints task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: a notebook or document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: this task sheet's three-part inventory prompts

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner fills out a three-part inventory: activities they are genuinely curious about or enjoy, strengths they can back with a specific remembered moment rather than a guess, and real constraints on time and getting to a location that they can name honestly.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact identifying interests, strengths, and constraints decision or action.
Model move 2: List five activities you are genuinely curious about or enjoy, in or out of school.
Model move 3: Name three personal strengths, and for each one describe one specific remembered moment that shows it, not just a claim.

Model check: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason. | Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment. | Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option.

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for identifying interests, strengths, and constraints.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner fills out a three-part inventory: activities they are genuinely curious about or enjoy, strengths they can back with a specific remembered moment rather than a guess, and real constraints on time and getting to a location that they can name honestly.
Coach direction: List five activities you are genuinely curious about or enjoy, in or out of school.
Learner prompt: List five activities, and for each one write a half-sentence on what specifically draws you to it.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Name three personal strengths, and for each one describe one specific remembered moment that shows it, not just a claim.
Response 1 (t2-p1): For each of three strengths, describe a specific moment where the strength actually showed up, not a general claim like 'I'm a hard worker.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): Each strength is backed by a specific remembered moment, not only a claim.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which constraint is the biggest open question for you right now, and why does it matter for the kind of work you'd realistically be able to start?

Success checks: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason. | Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment. | Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional identifying interests, strengths, and constraints condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason. | Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment. | Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner fills out a three-part inventory: activities they are genuinely curious about or enjoy, strengths they can back with a specific remembered moment rather than a guess, and real constraints on time and getting to a location that they can name honestly.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: List five activities, and for each one write a half-sentence on what specifically draws you to it.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: identifying interests, strengths, and constraints — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the identifying interests, strengths, and constraints task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which constraint is the biggest open question for you right now, and why does it matter for the kind of work you'd realistically be able to start?
observableCriteria: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason.
Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment.
Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of interests: Most activities include a specific half-sentence reason. | Evidence-based strengths: At least two of three strengths are backed by a specific remembered moment. | Honesty about constraints: States a realistic weekly time estimate and names at least one real transportation option.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
